title: Lead Gaza relief and move swiftly to economic recovery and reconstruction
description: President Abbas's letter of designation of 14 March 2024 made this the government's first task: 'leading, maximizing and coordinating the relief efforts in the Gaza Strip, and transitioning swiftly and effectively from the required humanitarian relief to economic recovery, and then organizing the reconstruction'. Accepting the assignment the next day, Mustafa pledged to alleviate 'the suffering of our people, especially in the Gaza Strip' and to prepare 'from this moment for economic recovery and reconstruction operations'. The programme he presented on 28 March 2024 put a comprehensive plan for humanitarian aid and immediate relief for Gaza, and recovery and reconstruction in Gaza and the West Bank, at the top of its priorities.
reasoning: The government is involved in relief and in planning recovery: its ministries report shelters, tents and housing repairs in Gaza (23 shelters prepared and about 800 damaged homes rehabilitated, the cabinet said on 20 October 2026), and Mustafa co-chaired with the European Commission the Palestine Donor Group, where the EU launched in July 2026 a 'Team Gaza' early-recovery initiative of about €900 million. Reconstruction itself has not begun: the final EU–UN–World Bank damage and needs assessment of April 2026 put needs at $71.4 billion over ten years and said minimum conditions such as a sustained ceasefire and adequate security were required, and under the US-backed plan Gaza's reconstruction is overseen by the Board of Peace and a technocratic committee rather than the PA. Concrete steps have been taken, but the PA does not lead the effort it was mandated to lead.
key_evidence: 14 March 2024: letter of designation makes Gaza relief, recovery and reconstruction the first task
15 March 2024: Mustafa's acceptance letter pledges relief and preparation for reconstruction 'from this moment'
20 April 2026: EU–UN Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment puts recovery and reconstruction needs at $71.4 billion, $26.3 billion in the first 18 months
13 July 2026: EU 'Team Gaza' early-recovery package of about €900 million announced at the donor group co-chaired by Mustafa
20 October 2026: cabinet reports shelter and housing repair work in Gaza and warns of cuts in relief funding (WFP suspending aid to about 500,000 people)

title: Reunify the institutions of Gaza and the West Bank and restore the PA's responsibilities in Gaza
description: The letter of designation asked the government to 'develop plans and implementation mechanisms for the reunification of institutions across the homeland's governorates as a single geographical, political, national, and institutional unit'. Mustafa repeated the goal as Prime Minister: at the Palestine Donor Group on 20 November 2025 he said reunification 'under a single legitimate government, one legal system, and one unified governance is not a slogan', and in Brussels on 20 April 2026 he called for transitional arrangements under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 that would enable the PA 'to fully assume its responsibilities in the Gaza Strip'.
reasoning: The PA has taken steps: in February 2026 it set up a liaison office headed by Mustafa to coordinate with the Board of Peace's High Representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, and in April 2026 Mustafa announced a committee in his office to prepare 'the transfer of the administration of Gaza to the Palestinian Authority at the end of the transitional phase'; local elections were also held in Deir al-Balah in April 2026. But under the US 20-point plan endorsed by Resolution 2803, Gaza's civil administration was given to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, which includes no PA or Hamas members, and the PA's return depends on completing its reforms; the July 2026 disarmament roadmap again assigns civil administration to that committee. The institutions remain divided; the end of the transition has no fixed date, hence the low confidence.
key_evidence: 14 March 2024: letter of designation asks for plans to reunify institutions
20 November 2025: Mustafa calls reunification under one government 'the practical pathway to peace'
January 2026: technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza announced, without PA members, based in Egypt (House of Commons Library)
21 February 2026: PA liaison office headed by Mustafa set up to coordinate with the High Representative
20 April 2026: Mustafa announces a committee in the Prime Minister's Office to manage the transfer of Gaza's administration to the PA
31 July 2026: Board of Peace disarmament roadmap leaves civil administration to the national committee (Al Jazeera)

title: Carry out the government's institutional reform agenda, to be completed by the end of 2026
description: The programme presented on 28 March 2024 included institutional reform, restructuring and unification of institutions, the fight against corruption, better services and digital transformation, as well as the rule of law, financial-sector integrity and the judiciary. The reform agenda was later agreed with the European Union and other donors as the 'National Program for Development and Reform'. On 20 April 2026 Mustafa said more than 70% of the reform plan had been completed and that it 'will be finalized by the end of this year'.
reasoning: Measures have been taken: the government cites a unified needs-based social protection law, VAT and tax reforms, the merger and dissolution of several institutions, renewed security leadership, merit-based competitive senior appointments and education reforms, and reported in July 2026 progress on 53 reform milestones in four pillars, 'with most agreed reforms completed'. EU Commissioner Dubravka Šuica thanked the government for its 'commitment to reform'. The AMAN Coalition (the national chapter of Transparency International) found 'positive indicators' and progress on parts of the agenda in its 2025 report, but also a continued concentration of power, patronage in appointments and weak oversight bodies. The end-2026 deadline has not passed and most progress figures come from the government itself.
key_evidence: 28 March 2024: programme with institutional reform, anti-corruption and digital transformation
20 November 2025: Mustafa tells the donor group institutions were merged and dissolved and senior appointments made merit-based
20 April 2026: 'over 70%' of the reform plan completed, to be finalised by the end of 2026
13 July 2026: progress reported on 53 milestones across four pillars
AMAN 2025 report: positive indicators, but concentration of power and patronage persist

title: Fight corruption and build a transparent, accountable system of governance
description: The letter of designation, to which the government's programme responded, asked it to aim for 'a robust and transparent governance system subject to accountability, combating corruption, and ensuring good governance', and the programme listed the fight against corruption among its reform priorities. On the day the cabinet was approved, the US State Department said it had encouraged the PA to implement reforms that 'crack down on corruption, increase transparency'.
reasoning: The AMAN Coalition's report on 2025 credits progress on parts of the reform agenda, more openness to civil society, improved procedures for appointing deputy ministers, the publication of 20 draft laws for consultation and spending held within the 2025 budget ceiling. It also records 84 appointments and 46 promotions to senior civilian and security posts and 40 ambassadors appointed in 2025, some with close ties to officials, weak compliance with conflict-of-interest disclosure, no right-to-information law, only 10 of 42 public institutions publishing annual reports, a weak Public Prosecution and an Anti-Corruption Commission that consults the presidency on cases involving influential figures. Mustafa says anti-corruption measures have been strengthened. Some steps are documented, but independent assessments are mixed.
key_evidence: 29 March 2024: State Department calls for reforms that 'crack down on corruption, increase transparency'
20 November 2025: Mustafa says anti-corruption measures were strengthened
AMAN 2025 report: 84 senior appointments and 46 promotions despite austerity; 10 of 42 institutions publish annual reports
AMAN 2025 report: no right-to-information law and weak conflict-of-interest disclosure

title: Stabilise the Palestinian Authority's finances
description: The government's programme of March 2024 included 'focusing efforts on stabilizing the financial situation and its economic impact', and the letter of designation asked for the 'rationalization of expenditures'. At the time public employees were already receiving reduced salaries.
reasoning: The PA's finances deteriorated sharply instead of stabilising. Israel's Finance Ministry, under Bezalel Smotrich, stopped transferring the clearance revenues it collects for the PA in 2025, citing the PA's 'actions against the State of Israel in the international arena and its support for incitement to terrorism'; it confirmed in April 2026 that nothing had been transferred for about a year, and the PA cabinet said in October 2026 that the revenues, 68% of public revenue, had been withheld for more than 18 months. May 2025 salaries were paid only at the end of July, June 2025 salaries at 50% (minimum NIS 2,000) in September 2025, January 2026 salaries only as NIS 2,000 in April 2026, and on 20 October 2026 the finance minister was still working to secure a salary payment. The government attributes the crisis mainly to the withholding, which Israel links to PA policies; whatever the cause, the commitment has not been delivered and cannot be while the revenues are withheld.
key_evidence: September 2025: school year postponed by a week; June salaries paid at 50% with a NIS 2,000 minimum (The Times of Israel)
19 April 2026: PA Finance Ministry announces January salaries will be limited to NIS 2,000
27 April 2026: Israel's Finance Ministry confirms no clearance revenues transferred to the PA for about a year
13 July 2026: Mustafa tells donors the economy has contracted by 30% since October 2023 and unemployment has reached 50%
AMAN 2025 report: spending kept within the budget ceiling, but shorter working hours hurt health, education and social protection
20 October 2026: cabinet says clearance revenues withheld for more than a year and a half

title: Replace payments to prisoners and families of those killed with a single needs-based social protection system
description: President Abbas's decree of 10 February 2025 ended the system under which the PA paid Palestinians held in Israeli prisons according to the length of their sentences, and the families of those killed or wounded in the conflict (whom the PA calls martyrs), including in attacks on Israelis; Israel and the US call this system 'pay for slay'. Assistance was moved to the needs-based programme of the Palestinian National Economic Empowerment Institution (Tamkeen). Mustafa's government is responsible for implementing the change, which he presents as 'the most significant overhaul of Palestine's social protection system in decades', a single needs-based framework under Decree-Law No. 4 of 2025 overseen by an independent supervisory body.
reasoning: The new system is in place and its completeness is disputed. In November 2025 a batch of payments was made under the old mechanism; in November 2025 Finance Minister Omar al-Bitar was replaced by Estephan Salameh without official explanation, after what Palestinian officials told The Times of Israel was an internal probe into payments he approved outside the new criteria. An audit commissioned by the PA from Alvarez & Marsal, whose summary was released in July 2026, found that the new programme had largely been separated from the old one but that more documentation was needed to verify that the old channels were closed. The US State Department called the reform an attempt to 'dupe' the international community through 'clandestine bypass channels', without providing evidence (The Times of Israel), and Israel says the payments continue; families of prisoners have protested the loss of stipends. Concrete steps have been taken but completion is not independently established, hence the low confidence.
key_evidence: 10 February 2025: decree ending sentence-based payments and moving assistance to Tamkeen
November 2025: Finance Minister Omar al-Bitar replaced after payments under the old system
20 November 2025: Mustafa says the Social Protection Law is in force with a national registry and external audits
July 2026: Alvarez & Marsal audit summary released; State Department dismisses it
13 July 2026: Mustafa presents Decree-Law No. 4 of 2025 as a unified, needs-based framework

title: Hold local elections in April 2026 under a new local elections law
description: At the Palestine Donor Group meeting in Brussels on 20 November 2025 Mustafa said: 'The Council of Ministers has approved a new Local Council Elections Law, and the Central Elections Commission will administer and oversee local elections scheduled for April 2026.' The PA said holding a vote in the Gaza Strip as well was meant to show that Gaza is an inseparable part of a future Palestinian state.
reasoning: Elections for 403 local authorities were held on 25 April 2026 in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah, the only part of the Gaza Strip that voted and the first Palestinian vote held in Gaza since 2006. Turnout was 53.5% overall (56% in the West Bank, 23% in Gaza, according to the Central Elections Commission chairman, Rami Hamdallah). Mustafa called the vote 'an important first step in a broader national process'. Hamas did not formally take part, many Fatah candidates in the West Bank ran unopposed, and the requirement that candidates commit to the PLO programme was criticised (see polemics). The elections were held as announced, though only one locality in Gaza took part.
key_evidence: 20 November 2025: new Local Council Elections Law approved by the Council of Ministers; elections announced for April 2026
25 April 2026: local elections in 403 local authorities, including Deir al-Balah
Turnout 53.5% (56% West Bank, 23% Gaza) according to the Central Elections Commission chairman
26 April 2026: Mustafa's press conference marking the end of the elections (The Times of Israel)

title: Prepare legislative and presidential elections 'as soon as possible'
description: The letter of designation, which served as the government's mandate in the absence of a sitting Legislative Council, asked it to take 'the necessary measures and preparations for holding legislative and presidential elections in the northern governorates, including East Jerusalem, and the southern governorates, as soon as possible in accordance with the Basic Law'. No national election had been held since 2006.
reasoning: Preparations were made: Mustafa told donors in July 2026 that President Abbas had issued a decree calling Legislative Council elections for 28 November 2026, with a presidential election expected in early 2027. But on 10 October 2026 Abbas postponed both to 11 September 2027; the PLO Executive Committee said conditions were not conducive, citing Israeli restrictions in Gaza and East Jerusalem, military raids, settler violence and the withholding of tax revenues, while Israel's foreign minister accused Abbas of 'fooling the international community'. The decision to postpone was the President's, not the government's. Two and a half years after the mandate, no national election has taken place; it is still scheduled, so the verdict is in progress with low confidence.
key_evidence: 14 March 2024: letter of designation asks for election preparations 'as soon as possible'
By July 2026: presidential decree calls legislative elections for 28 November 2026
10 October 2026: legislative and presidential elections postponed to 11 September 2027 (Al Jazeera, citing WAFA)

title: Guarantee freedom of the media and of expression
description: The letter of designation asked the government to ensure 'public and private freedoms in accordance with the law, most notably freedom of opinion and expression', and 'freedom of operation for media within the framework of applicable laws and regulations that guarantee freedom of movement and media activities, access to information sources, and social media'. The government's programme included 'ensuring public freedoms'.
reasoning: On 1 January 2025 a ministerial committee of the ministries of culture, interior and communications, according to WAFA, suspended Al Jazeera's broadcasts and froze the work of its journalists and crews in PA areas, accusing it of 'inciting material' in its coverage of the PA security operation in Jenin refugee camp; the UN human rights office, Reporters Without Borders and the Foreign Press Association criticised the order, which was lifted only after President Abbas's decision in May 2025. In September 2025 police arrested three people in Ramallah under a law on social-media incitement after an audio clip about the salary crisis circulated (The Times of Israel). AMAN's 2025 report records 'a continued decline in public freedoms and human rights'. The government's own committee imposed a four-month ban on a major broadcaster, which contradicts the commitment.
key_evidence: 1 January 2025: ministerial committee suspends Al Jazeera in PA areas
UN human rights office: 'reverse course and respect its international law obligations'
12 May 2025: lifting of the ban announced after a decision by Abbas
September 2025: three arrests in Ramallah over a viral audio clip about unpaid salaries
AMAN 2025 report: continued decline in public freedoms

title: Reform the security services into a professional, accountable force
description: The letter of designation asked the government to continue 'the reform process in all institutional, security, economic, administrative and public finance fields', and the programme included 'enhancing security and safety'. In Brussels on 20 April 2026 Mustafa said: 'Our efforts in reforming the security sector, with the support of our international partners, are focused on building a professional, civilian, and accountable security apparatus.'
reasoning: Mustafa said in November 2025 that the government had 'renewed security leadership', and AMAN's 2025 report notes legislative measures to restructure the security sector, including early retirement for a number of officers to reduce the wage bill, while saying the reform should extend to more ranks. The same report records the security agencies' refusal to enforce 50 final court rulings, notably on releasing detainees and reinstating employees, and the continued requirement of security clearance for access to some rights and services. Some steps are documented; independent information on the reform's scope is limited, hence the low confidence.
key_evidence: 20 November 2025: 'renewed security leadership' (Mustafa)
AMAN 2025 report: early retirement of officers to reduce the wage bill
AMAN 2025 report: security agencies did not enforce 50 final court rulings
20 April 2026: Mustafa describes the aim of a 'professional, civilian, and accountable' security apparatus
